question: On the S59 prime and the fixed NIST-shaped curve y^2=x^3-3x+11, how do intrinsic coordinate-defined factor bases differ in planted-relation admission, coordinate-evaluation cost, invariance, and isolated wall time; and how do all supported prime-field EFD model charts differ in exact straight-line arithmetic cost and round-trip support?

claims.text: Every admitted input triple is a planted zero-sum relation, the deliberately wrong triple is rejected, every reported chart round-trips, and every reported applicable addition or doubling agrees with the affine oracle.
The nine fixed-curve coordinate arms have measurably different factor-base density, planted-relation admission rate, invariance, or coordinate-evaluation cost on the frozen S59 fixture.
claims.if_supported: report the paired effect for each arm versus x, with algebraic degree and invariance shown beside the rate
claims.if_not_supported: report the arms as indistinguishable at this fixture and resolution; do not claim equivalence

claims.text: The supported EFD charts differ in exact straight-line field-operation counts; those counts describe representation engineering and do not by themselves establish a better index-calculus surface.
Plane-quartic and hyperelliptic coordinates are not compared as alternate coordinates of this elliptic-curve group without an explicit subgroup-preserving transfer, recovery map, and cost ledger.

hypotheses.statement: Degree-2 Kummer-equivalent x, normalized Jacobian x, and Mobius-x arms will have comparable density-adjusted planted-relation admission; differences should be constant-factor extraction cost or threshold placement rather than a new asymptotic surface.
hypotheses.mechanism: They represent the same degree-2 quotient function up to normalization or a fractional-linear change of variable.

predictions.minimum_effect: a Holm-corrected paired 95% interval excluding ratio 1 and exceeding the x/x_aa control spread

data_seen.measured: prior literature/lead synthesis only; no output from this Rust instrument

arms.description: Affine x-coordinate factor base, the degree-2 Kummer reference.
Byte-for-byte repeated x-coordinate extraction under a distinct arm identifier.
Projective X normalized by Z squared; mathematically the same affine x function with explicit inversion cost.
Raw projective X with independently varied scale; it must fail scale invariance and is not a curve function.
Affine y-coordinate, a degree-3 curve function with different negation behavior.
Affine x+y, a degree-3 curve function.
The degree-4 composition x squared, included to expose image collisions and extraction cost.
The rational function x/y, with poles recorded explicitly.
All 33 supported prime-field EFD charts across ten models; only exact round-trip, affine-oracle agreement, and straight-line counts are cross-chart evidence.

positive.not_applicable_reason: every sampled row constructs R=-(P+Q) and the harness verifies (P+Q)+R is infinity, so the positive detector is exercised on every arm rather than as a separate arm

null_population.description: the same affine points re-encoded under two independently derived nonzero projective scales
null_population.generator: splitmix64(seed, sample index, domain separator) modulo p, with zero replaced by one
null_population.why_n: 8 seeds times 262144 triples times 3 points gives exact scale-invariance resolution below one part per million

factors.name: field
factors.how: one registry prime shared by all arms

factors.name: primary curve
factors.how: one NIST-shaped short-Weierstrass fixture; no curve-order or subgroup-order claim

factors.name: seeded traces
factors.how: eight protocol-hash-derived seeds, shared across coordinate arms

factors.name: coordinate arm
factors.how: every seeded trace is evaluated under all nine coordinate definitions

factors.name: factor-base threshold
factors.how: identical numeric threshold for all coordinate images

factors.name: chart parameter fixture
factors.how: one explicit valid parameter set per EFD model/chart; the birationally produced short-Weierstrass curve is recorded

factors.name: host load
factors.how: CPU, kernel, isolation, steal, PSI, worker count, and binary hash are recorded for timed rows

required_before_comparison: explicit subgroup-preserving map from the elliptic target group
recovery map back to the elliptic target
kernel, image, exceptional-set, and cofactor accounting
transfer and recovery cost included in every metric

randomization.arm_order_reason: counting rows are deterministic; isolated timed rows alternate arm order within each seed to limit drift

seed_derivation.note: eight fixed u64 seeds chosen before affected data; every coordinate arm receives the same seed at a given instance index

instance_sampling.rule: eight deterministic P,Q traces derived from the protocol seed; each trace advances P by 2G and Q by 3G for exactly 262144 samples

blinding.how: not masked because invariance and algebraic degree are explicit coordinate properties and exact counters dominate the engineering comparison

power.note: each arm receives 6291456 coordinate evaluations per eight-seed pass and roughly 512 admitted triples at density 1/16; this resolves large admission effects, while exact invariance and operation counts need no sampling inference

primary.name: relation and chart correctness
primary.definition: planted and wrong relation oracles, chart encode/decode/re-encode equality, and applicable chart arithmetic equality with the affine oracle
primary.source: relation rows planted_zero_sum_passes and negative_zero_sum_failures; chart rows status and verified_cases

primary.name: planted-relation admission rate
primary.definition: a triple is admitted only when all three coordinate images are defined and below floor(p/16)

primary.name: density-adjusted relation admission
primary.definition: observed planted-relation admission divided by the cube of the observed single-coordinate density; descriptive dependence diagnostic, not a full relation-generation success rate

primary.name: coordinate extraction field operations
primary.definition: multiplications, squarings, inversions, and additions required to extract the coordinate value; elliptic point generation and factor-base comparison are excluded

primary.name: EFD straight-line field operations
primary.unit: field operations by class per formula
primary.definition: compiled straight-line formula multiplications, squarings, inversions, and additions; chart conversion, qualification, and validation are excluded

secondary.name: isolated wall time
secondary.definition: monotonic time around the frozen relation or chart batch after one warmup; admissible only for a single-worker arm in an L2 isolated run
secondary.source: relation rows wall_ns and chart formula wall_ns

placement.counting: local or throughput workers; four workers per batch
placement.timing: IsoLab/EKS L2 isolated pods; one worker per arm, pods parallel across seeds and arms

stopping_rules.rule: fixed counting design: eight seeds times nine coordinate arms at 262144 triples per arm, plus all EFD chart rows, then stop
fixed timing design: one warmup and five measured repetitions per seed and arm, then stop
stop and classify the affected arm invalid if a planted relation fails, a wrong relation is accepted, a chart reports a false verified status, or a binary/commit mismatch is observed

invalidation_rules: a wall-time row with workers other than one or isolation below L2 is descriptive only and cannot support a speed claim
an arm with any planted relation failure or wrong-relation acceptance is invalid rather than slow
a chart without a valid parameter fixture or supported round-trip is reported inapplicable/unsupported and excluded from arithmetic ranking
any row whose binary hash or commit differs from the frozen instrument is invalid
counted units remain valid across hosts when the binary and input hashes match

decision_rule.text: C2 is supported descriptively for an arm when its paired effect versus x on relation rate or density-adjusted rate has a Holm-corrected 95% bootstrap interval excluding ratio 1 and exceeds the x/x_aa control spread, or when its exact extraction-cost or invariance vector differs. Algebraic-degree and invariance differences must be reported and forbid a blanket superiority claim.
decision_rule.threshold: Holm-corrected interval excludes 1 and effect exceeds A/A for sampled rates; any nonzero exact difference for counts or invariance
decision_rule.statistic: paired candidate/x ratio by seed for rates; exact vector difference for operation counts and invariance
decision_rule.interval: paired bootstrap across eight seeded traces, 95%, with x/x_aa as the control distribution
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: rate ratio and absolute percentage-point difference; field-operation vector; invariance-match fraction

graphs: coordinate relation rate and density-adjusted rate with x/x_aa control
EFD addition and doubling straight-line operation counts

inadmissible: changing seeds, threshold, curve, coordinate definitions, sample count, or stopping rule after seeing affected data
quoting local or multi-worker wall time as a benchmark result
calling raw projective X an intrinsic coordinate or factor-base function
treating projective storage charts as new index-calculus surfaces
ranking different curve models as the same ECDLP target when no explicit isomorphism or subgroup-preserving transfer is included
including plane-quartic or hyperelliptic results in the elliptic fixed-group comparison without the registered transfer obligations
claiming a sub-square-root ECDLP algorithm or extrapolating the S59 fixture to NIST security sizes
using a different-language compute implementation for new experiment code
